_readme: Parameter reference for config/models/ollama/llama3.2.3b.json (and any other config/models/<provider>/*.json file that follows the same Ollama shape). This file is documentation only — Mova never reads it. Each key below mirrors a real field from llama3.2.3b.json, with its type, default/example value, and what it controls. See docs/i18n/en/PROJECT_JSON.md and docs/i18n/en/COMMANDS.md § 6 for how this file is referenced from project.json's llm_profile.config.

base_url.description: Where the Ollama server is reachable. localhost for a model running on this same machine; a private-network address (Tailscale/WireGuard IP, or a cloud VPC's internal IP) for a remote/centralized server — see config/models/ollama/llama3.2.3b-remote.json for that variant and docs/i18n/en/DEPLOY.md for the full deployment guide. Never point this at an unprotected public IP.

timeout_seconds.description: How long Mova waits for a response before giving up. Local models on modest hardware can be slow on the first call (model load into memory) — 300s is a safe default; lower it for small/fast models, raise it for large models or slow hardware.

model.description: The exact model tag Ollama should run, in Ollama's own "name:tag" format — must match a model already pulled with `ollama pull` (or `mova install`, which wraps the same API).

top_k.description: Limits token sampling to the K most likely next tokens. Lower values (e.g. 10-20) make output more focused/deterministic; higher values (e.g. 80-100) allow more variety. 40 is Ollama's own sensible default.

top_p.description: Nucleus sampling: only considers tokens whose cumulative probability mass is <= top_p. Works alongside top_k as a second filter. 0.9 is a common balanced default; lower it (e.g. 0.5) for more deterministic output.

num_ctx.description: The context window Ollama actually allocates for THIS run, in tokens — distinct from context_window below (see that field's description for the difference). Must be large enough to hold the assembled context Mova sends, or the model will silently truncate the oldest part of it.

threads.description: CPU threads Ollama uses for inference on this model. Roughly: physical CPU cores minus 1-2 reserved for the OS/other processes. Irrelevant if Ollama is running with GPU acceleration for this model, but harmless to leave set.

mirostat.description: Ollama's adaptive-perplexity sampling mode: 0 = disabled (use top_k/top_p instead, the common choice), 1 = Mirostat, 2 = Mirostat 2.0. Leave at 0 unless you specifically want Mirostat's perplexity-targeting behavior.

keep_alive.description: How long Ollama keeps this model loaded in memory after the last request, before unloading it to free RAM/VRAM. "24h" keeps it warm for a full day of use (no reload latency on the next call); "0" unloads immediately after each response; "5m" is Ollama's own default.

num_predict.description: Maximum number of tokens the model may generate in its reply (the output-token cap). This is the ONLY place this project sets a per-model output limit — see llama3.2.3b.json's own file header comment on why LLMProfile no longer duplicates a "max_tokens" field.

temperature.description: Sampling randomness: 0 = fully deterministic (same input -> same output, ideal for analysis/extraction tasks like this project's own examples), up to ~1.0+ for more creative/varied output. This project's default examples use 0 because audit/compliance tasks need reproducibility.

context_window.description: The model's own architectural maximum context length (what the model CAN theoretically support), used by Mova's Budget/Token Firewall (see budget/ and models.UsageFor) to warn before a request would exceed it. Distinct from num_ctx (what Ollama actually allocates for a given run, which can be smaller than this ceiling to save memory).

repeat_penalty.description: Penalizes tokens the model has already used recently, discouraging repetitive loops. 1.0 = no penalty; 1.1-1.3 is a common range for noticeably reducing repetition without hurting coherence.

stream.description: Whether the model streams tokens as they're generated (true, what `mova chat`'s REPL uses for a live typing effect) or returns the full response only once generation finishes (false, simpler for a one-shot API call like the MCP/HTTP chat_completion tool).

_type_field_note: Some provider configs (e.g. LM Studio's lfm2.5-1.2b.json) also carry a top-level "type" field ("openai", "ollama", "anthropic"...) identifying which HTTP wire protocol to speak, plus an "api_key" field when the endpoint requires one. Ollama's own native API needs neither — both are omitted from a plain Ollama config like this one.
